project: EchoDrop - British English shadowing game (Android + Soniox)

features.name: Account and cloud sync
features.description: Email/password account. Sentence bank, attempts and progress are stored server-side and synced to the device, so the same bank appears on a second device after login.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/auth/signup with a new email returns 201 and a token; repeating the same email returns 409.
POST /api/auth/login with correct credentials returns 200 and a token; wrong password returns 401.
Any request to an endpoint other than E1/E2 without a valid Authorization bearer token returns 401.
After importing sentences on device A, GET /api/sentences with device B's token for the same account returns the identical sentence ids and texts.
GET /api/sentences with account X's token never returns a row whose user_id is not X.

features.name: Paste-to-bank sentence import
features.description: A screen with one large multi-line text box. The user pastes sentences separated by newlines; the app splits per line, trims whitespace, drops empty lines, deduplicates against the existing bank by normalized text, and adds the rest to a deck.
acceptance_criteria: Pasting a block of N non-empty lines and submitting creates exactly N sentences when none already exist in the bank.
Lines that are empty or whitespace-only are skipped and never create a sentence.
Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped from every stored sentence text.
Re-submitting a block whose lines are already in the bank creates 0 new sentences and the response reports them under skipped_duplicates.
Deduplication is case-insensitive and punctuation-insensitive: 'Hello there.' and 'hello there' are treated as the same sentence.
A single line longer than 300 characters is rejected and reported in the response's rejected array without aborting the rest of the import.
After a successful import the bank screen lists the new sentences without requiring an app restart.

features.name: British-accent sentence playback
features.description: Each sentence can be played aloud in a British English voice via the Soniox Text-to-Speech API. Generated audio is cached server-side per (sentence, voice, model) and cached again on the device, so a repeat play makes no network call.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/tts for a sentence returns 200 with an audio asset reference and a duration_ms greater than 0.
The default voice used is a British-accent voice and is one of Oliver, Arthur, Isla, Victoria.
Calling POST /api/tts twice for the same sentence_id and voice returns the same audio_id and issues only one upstream Soniox TTS request (verified from the server's upstream-call counter or log).
After a sentence has been played once, playing it again with the device in airplane mode still produces audio from the device cache.
The user can change the voice in settings and the next playback uses the newly selected voice.

features.name: Speak and be scored
features.description: The user taps the microphone and repeats the sentence. Device audio is streamed to the Soniox real-time speech-to-text WebSocket, tokens stream back and are highlighted live against the target sentence. On stop, the final tokens are sent to the backend, which computes the authoritative score.
acceptance_criteria: The app never contains a long-lived Soniox API key: the only Soniox credential it holds is one obtained from POST /api/stt/temp-key, and grepping the built APK for the account API key finds no match.
POST /api/stt/temp-key returns a key whose expiry is at most 300 seconds in the future.
Recording without microphone permission shows a permission prompt and does not open a WebSocket.
While the user speaks, partial tokens appear in the UI within 1000 ms of the corresponding speech, before the user stops recording.
Words of the target sentence that were recognized are marked matched and words that were not are marked missed, per the scoring alignment.
POST /api/attempts with a transcript identical to the sentence returns accuracy 1.0 and stars 3.
POST /api/attempts with an empty transcript returns accuracy 0.0 and stars 0.
If the WebSocket drops mid-recording, the app shows a retry affordance and no attempt row is created.

features.name: Scoring, stars and progression
features.description: Deterministic server-side scoring. Reference and hypothesis are normalized (lowercased, punctuation stripped, whitespace collapsed) and aligned word by word. accuracy = matched_words / reference_words. confidence_avg = mean confidence of matched tokens. pace_ratio = spoken_duration_ms / reference_duration_ms. Stars: 3 when accuracy >= 0.95 and confidence_avg >= 0.80; 2 when accuracy >= 0.80; 1 when accuracy >= 0.60; otherwise 0. score = round(700*accuracy + 200*confidence_avg + 100*pace_bonus), where pace_bonus = max(0, 1 - abs(pace_ratio - 1)). A sentence is mastered once it has been scored 3 stars at least twice.
acceptance_criteria: The scoring function is pure and deterministic: the same reference, tokens and durations produce the same score on repeated calls.
Scoring is case-insensitive and punctuation-insensitive: transcript 'hello there' against reference 'Hello, there!' yields accuracy 1.0.
accuracy is always between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive, and stars is always an integer in 0..3, for every input including empty and longer-than-reference transcripts.
A transcript missing exactly one word out of ten yields accuracy 0.9 and stars 2.
score is an integer between 0 and 1000 inclusive.
Only the highest star count a sentence has ever earned is kept in progress.best_stars; a later worse attempt does not lower it.
GET /api/progress total_stars equals the sum of best_stars across that user's sentences.
A sentence reaches mastered true only after two attempts of 3 stars, and never before.

features.name: Cut-the-Rope-styled game presentation
features.description: Visual language borrowed from Cut the Rope: warm cardboard and wood backgrounds, thick rounded shapes, chunky playful display type, a bouncy candy-drop and star-burst animation on a scored attempt, and a level-tile map for the bank. Mechanics stay simple: one sentence per card, listen, repeat, earn up to 3 stars.
acceptance_criteria: Every screen listed in ui_screens renders on a 360x640 dp screen with no clipped or overlapping text and no horizontal scrolling.
Completing an attempt plays a star-burst animation whose star count equals the stars value returned by POST /api/attempts.
The home map shows one tile per sentence, and each tile displays that sentence's best_stars as 0 to 3 filled stars.
All interactive controls are at least 48x48 dp.
The app has no unstyled default Material surfaces on the play screen: background, card and buttons all use the project's own theme tokens.

features.name: Offline resilience
features.description: The sentence bank, cached TTS audio and unsent attempts live in a local database. With no network the user can still review and replay previously played sentences; attempts made offline are queued and pushed on reconnect.
acceptance_criteria: With the network disabled, launching the app shows the previously synced sentence bank rather than an error screen.
An attempt recorded while offline is stored locally and appears on the server after the network returns, without user action.
A queued attempt is never submitted twice: after a reconnect, the server holds exactly one row per queued attempt (verified by its client-generated idempotency key).

features.name: Reproducible Android build in CI
features.description: A GitHub Actions workflow builds the Android app and runs the unit test suites for both the app and the backend on every push, publishing the debug APK as a build artifact.
acceptance_criteria: The workflow runs on ubuntu-24.04 and completes assembleDebug with exit code 0.
The workflow uploads an .apk file as a downloadable artifact.
The workflow runs the Android unit tests and the backend test suite, and fails the job if either fails.
The build requires no Soniox credentials: it succeeds with no Soniox secret configured in the repository.

assumptions: Platform is a native Android app (Kotlin) plus an HTTP backend; the user chose CI-based APK builds because the local build environment has no Android SDK access.

The visual reference is Cut the Rope's look and feel only (colors, shapes, typography, star rewards). No rope-cutting physics, no Om Nom character, and no ZeptoLab assets are reproduced; all art is original.
Soniox is used for both halves of the loop: Text-to-Speech for the British-accent prompt and real-time Speech-to-Text for the learner's repetition. Verified against the official soniox-python SDK.

The account Soniox API key lives only on the backend. The Android client receives short-lived temporary keys minted via Soniox POST /auth/temporary-api-key with usage_type transcribe_websocket. The TTS path is proxied through the backend rather than given a temporary key, so audio can be cached and billed once per sentence.

Exact Soniox model identifiers for STT and TTS are read at runtime from the Soniox model-listing endpoints and supplied to the client via E10 and E13, rather than hardcoded, because api.soniox.com was unreachable from the planning environment and could not be verified live.

Default TTS voice is a British-accent built-in voice; the four British voices seen in the official Soniox OpenAPI document are Oliver, Arthur, Isla and Victoria. The live list is confirmed at runtime through E13.
Device audio is captured as 16 kHz mono PCM signed 16-bit little-endian and streamed to the Soniox real-time WebSocket in that format.

Soniox does not expose phoneme-level pronunciation assessment. Scoring is therefore word-alignment accuracy plus recognition confidence plus pace, not a true pronunciation score. If phoneme-level scoring is required, a different vendor must be added.
Authentication is email plus password with bearer tokens. No third-party OAuth provider was requested.

The backend is the existing Next.js application in this repository, extended with the endpoints above; the specific database and hosting provider are an implementation choice left to the Backend role.
Sentences are English. Multi-language decks are out of scope for this spec.
Audio of the learner's own voice is not stored server-side; only the resulting transcript and scores are.
Target is phone-sized portrait Android; tablet and landscape layouts are out of scope.
No monetization, no leaderboard and no social features are in scope.
